Why does this concrete tower survive?
Some attribute its survival to steel reinforcement.
But steel would have melted in the blaze.
Others point to various post-accident structural theories.
Those myths ignore the original design.
The chimney is a massive reinforced concrete shell.
Its thickness prevented collapse during the fire.
After the fire, only the crown was taken down.
Core contamination forced workers to leave the shaft sealed.
Decommissioning began in the 1980s, keeping it intact.
Thus the tower still dominates the Cumberland skyline.
Observers often look at the chimney standing in Cumbria.
